collection_method: Read-only GitHub repository, issue-search, issue and comment GET requests through the GitHub connector. Embedded code and reproductions were treated as evidence and not executed. No packages, SDKs, agents, A2A messages, webhooks, target systems, attachments or linked demonstrations were run or contacted.

scope.supporting_followup_outside_search_sampl: One directly cited public aws/bedrock-agentcore-sdk-python issue was read to assess the same context-isolation defect in a downstream integration; it is not counted among the 91 unique A2A-project issue URLs.

selected_records.title: [Bug]: DefaultRequestHandler runs follow-up messages on a task with the first request's contextvars
selected_records.provider_attribution: A2A Python SDK DefaultRequestHandler behavior; no model-provider execution is established.
selected_records.assessment: A deterministic two-turn reproduction reports that a follow-up message is processed by the task executor using the first request's context variables, including possible auth token, tenant or caller identity, while the per-message ServerCallContext remains correct. The follow-up input is received and used, but it is user input rather than a transferred task result. This is a newly published SDK isolation defect, not evidence of an autonomous swarm.

selected_records.title: [BUG] A2A (a2a-sdk 1.x): follow-up messages on an existing task run the executor with the first request's contextvars
selected_records.provider_attribution: AWS Bedrock AgentCore integration with A2A SDK 1.x; no Bedrock model execution or external service call is established by the local reproduction.
selected_records.assessment: A separate public report reproduces the same task-follow-up context bug through the Bedrock AgentCore SDK and says workload tokens and propagated authorization may remain from turn one. The repository labels it high severity and provides a local workaround. This corroborates impact in a downstream integration but remains a controlled SDK test, not a live peer exchange or swarm.

selected_records.title: Real-world evidence: undefined stream completion signal (see #1746) allows silent, undetectable truncation on a production A2A server
selected_records.provider_attribution: Reporter-tested Google Vertex AI Agent Engine and ADK A2A adapter; model/provider provenance is reporter-asserted.
selected_records.assessment: The reporter describes a deployed A2A stream delivering only part of an agent result and closing without a terminal state, while a non-A2A control returned the full response. This is production-shaped result-transfer evidence and a protocol reliability gap, but no unauthorized coordination or downstream result use is shown.

selected_records.title: [Bug]: Idempotency hole when sending first message
selected_records.provider_attribution: A2A protocol design discussion; no provider execution.
selected_records.assessment: The protocol discussion identifies a retry window in which a client may not know whether its first task started, creating potential duplicate work. No duplicate autonomous execution was observed; work moved to a consolidated specification issue.

selected_records.title: [Bug]: ResultManager:processEvents (second events modifies first arriving event) which leads to unexpected behavior and race conditions
selected_records.provider_attribution: A2A JavaScript SDK result aggregation; no model-provider attribution.
selected_records.assessment: A shared task object could be mutated by a later status event while an earlier response was still being returned. Maintainers reproduced the race and later closed it as fixed in 1.x. It is same-task state aliasing, not inter-agent result misdelivery.

selected_records.title: [Feat]: PushNotificationConfig.authentication is ignored; no Authorization header is sent in push notifications
selected_records.provider_attribution: A2A Python SDK push-notification sender; no provider execution.
selected_records.assessment: The SDK ignored a configured push-authentication field, preventing receivers from authenticating the sender as the specification described. A later pull request added support and the issue closed. This is an authentication control, not an observed unauthorized exchange.

novelty_result: No previously unreported rogue swarm confirmed. The newly filed A2A Python issue and its downstream AgentCore counterpart establish a material cross-request identity/token isolation defect in controlled tests, but no autonomous participants, task-result exchange or rogue intent.
limitations: Searches were capped at 20 newest-updated rows and overlap; this is not a complete issue census.
Issue bodies and comments are public assertions and local reproductions, not authenticated agent telemetry.
The two context-isolation reports use distinct public accounts and integrations but reference the same root cause; they are supporting records, not proof of independent live exploitation.
A follow-up user message processed under stale context is not itself a task result transferred between autonomous agents.
Open issue state and high-severity labeling establish tracker status, not ongoing autonomous activity.
No code, SDK, package, reproduction, agent, webhook, message or target service was executed or contacted.

Advancement requires an unpublished original exchange with independently corroborated autonomous participants, transferred task work actually used by a distinguishable recipient, and evidence that the coordination itself crossed operator authorization in a real run.
redactions: No raw credentials, tokens, authorization headers, executable reproduction bodies, private logs, webhook destinations or personal addresses are included.
Assessments retain public record links, timestamps and body hashes while summarizing security mechanics at a domain level.
